name: ZITLAS Paneer Tikka Skewers
description: Paneer cubes marinated in curd and spices, grilled on skewers — a tikka format eaten as breakfast rather than an evening starter.
instructions: Marinate paneer, capsicum and onion cubes in curd and tikka masala for at least 15 minutes.
Thread onto skewers, alternating paneer and vegetables.
Grill in an oven or air fryer at 200°C for 10-12 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Grilled, not fried — very little added oil
Skewer format is genuinely different from any bhurji, roll or toast in the database
High protein for a light breakfast

name: ZITLAS Moong Cheela Veg Taco Fold
description: A moong dal cheela folded taco-style around a fresh, no-cook vegetable salsa — the filling is raw and crunchy rather than cooked.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 60 g
instructions: Cook the moong dal batter into a small, sturdy round on the tawa (thicker than a regular cheela so it holds a fold).
Toss tomato, onion and cucumber with lemon juice and coriander for a fresh salsa.
Fold the warm cheela in half like a taco shell and spoon in the raw salsa just before eating so it stays crisp.
Eat immediately.
why_it_works: Combining a cooked base with a raw, no-cook filling is a distinct format from every other cheela in the database
Very fresh, crunchy texture contrast
Light and low-calorie

name: ZITLAS Baked Vegetable Frittata Slice
description: A single large egg-and-vegetable frittata baked in one pan and cut into slices — different from individual muffin cups, meant to be sliced and shared or portioned.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C and grease a round baking dish.
Saute onion, capsicum and spinach in oil for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, then pour over the vegetables in the greased dish.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until fully set and lightly golden on top.
Cool slightly, slice like a pie, and serve.
why_it_works: One large bake serves multiple people, unlike single-portion muffin cups
Slices reheat well for a couple of days
Good option for a shared family breakfast

name: ZITLAS Chana Pulao Bowl
description: A lightly spiced rice pulao cooked with boiled chana — a warm rice-and-legume breakfast bowl, distinct from a khichdi or curry-rice pairing.
ingredients: Whole spices (bay leaf, cumin), garam masala — 4 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper whole spices, then saute onion until golden.
Add rice and boiled chana, along with garam masala, mixing well.
Add water in the standard rice ratio and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.
why_it_works: Pulao format (whole grains of rice, not mushy like khichdi) is a genuinely different texture from other rice-legume dishes here
One-pot, mostly hands-off cooking
Filling for a mid-morning appetite

name: ZITLAS Chana Masala Toast Boats
description: Whole wheat bread rolls hollowed out and filled with a scoop of hot chana masala — a boat format distinct from a flat toast topping.
ingredients: Chana masala powder, ginger-garlic paste — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook until soft.
Add boiled chana and chana masala powder with a little water; simmer 8-10 minutes into a thick masala.
Slice the top off each bread roll and hollow out some of the inside to make a boat.
Spoon the hot chana masala into the bread boats and serve immediately.
why_it_works: Boat format holds a wet curry without making the bread soggy the way a flat toast topping would
Fun, different presentation of a familiar chana masala
High fiber from chana and bread combined

name: ZITLAS Roasted Flaxseed Peanut Bites
description: No-bake bites made from roasted flaxseed powder and peanuts bound with jaggery — a different seed base from the chikki or ladoo bites elsewhere, adding an omega-3 angle.
instructions: Melt jaggery with ghee in a kadai on low heat until syrupy.
Turn off heat, quickly mix in ground flaxseed and crushed peanuts, coating evenly.
Shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Cool completely and store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Flaxseed brings a fiber and omega-3 profile that the peanut-only or besan-only bites in the database don't have
Genuinely different base ingredient, not just a renamed chikki
Batch-made for the week

name: ZITLAS Paneer Stuffed Naan Bites
description: Small naan breads stuffed with spiced paneer and cooked in a pan — a naan-based format, distinct from roti, kulcha or paratha stuffing elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Knead maida with curd, a pinch of baking soda and water into a soft dough; rest 20 minutes.
Mix paneer with onion and chaat masala for the filling.
Divide the dough into small balls, stuff each with a little filling and seal.
Flatten gently and roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden spots appear on both sides.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Naan dough (with curd and baking soda) has a distinctly softer, puffier texture from a plain wheat dough
Bite-sized format works well for sharing or a lunchbox
Broadens the bread formats in the database beyond roti/paratha/kulcha

name: ZITLAS Egg Drop Vegetable Soup Bowl
description: A light vegetable broth with beaten egg dropped in ribbons, Indo-Chinese style — a savoury liquid breakfast built around egg rather than dal.
ingredients: Garlic, black pepper, soy sauce — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute garlic and finely chopped vegetables for 2 minutes.
Add water and bring to a gentle boil; simmer 5 minutes.
Season with black pepper and soy sauce.
Beat the egg and pour in slowly in a thin stream while stirring, so it forms ribbons.
Serve hot in a bowl.
why_it_works: Egg-based soup format is distinct from the dal-based Green Moong Soup Bowl elsewhere in the database
Very light, good for a low-appetite morning
Quick, one-pot preparation

name: ZITLAS Sprouted Chana Chaat Bowl
description: Raw sprouted chana (not boiled) tossed with onion, tomato and lemon — a crunchier, no-cook alternative to boiled-chana-based chaats.
ingredients: Sprouted chana (raw sprouts, not boiled) — 100 g
instructions: Rinse the sprouted chana well.
Toss with onion, tomato, lemon juice and chaat masala.
Eat immediately for maximum crunch — sprouted chana softens if left standing.
why_it_works: Sprouted (raw) rather than boiled chana keeps a distinctly crunchier bite than the boiled versions used elsewhere
Entirely no-cook
High fiber, low calorie

name: ZITLAS Stuffed Multigrain Dosa
description: A multigrain dosa filled with a spiced paneer masala and folded closed — a stuffed dosa format distinct from a plain or topped dosa.
instructions: Mix multigrain flour into the fermented dosa batter.
Heat oil, saute onion until soft, add paneer, turmeric and chilli powder, cook 3-4 minutes for the filling.
Pour the batter on a hot tawa and spread into a dosa.
Once mostly cooked, place the paneer filling on one half and fold the dosa over.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Stuffed-and-folded construction is a genuinely different eating experience from a flat or topped dosa
Multigrain flour raises fiber above a plain rice-urad dosa
Filling protein source keeps this distinct from the plain Ragi Dosa or Vegetable Rava Idli

name: ZITLAS Dahi Poha
description: Cold flattened rice soaked directly in whisked curd with a light tempering — a chilled poha format, distinct from the hot tempered kanda poha or leftover rice poha.
instructions: Rinse the poha briefly and let it soften, then mix directly into whisked curd.
Add finely chopped onion and mix.
Quickly temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in a little hot oil and pour over the top.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
why_it_works: Cold, curd-based format is a genuinely different eating experience from hot tempered poha
Very light and cooling, good for hot weather
Almost no active cooking

name: ZITLAS Oats Banana Pancake Stack
description: Griddle-cooked pancakes made from a blended oats-and-banana batter, stacked like a Western-style pancake breakfast but without refined flour or added sugar.
instructions: Blend oats, banana, milk and egg together into a smooth, pourable batter.
Heat a lightly greased tawa and pour small rounds of batter, cooking 2 minutes per side until golden.
Stack 3-4 small pancakes.
Serve as is — the banana provides sweetness without any added sugar.
why_it_works: Griddle-pancake format is genuinely different from the smoothie bowl or porridge oats already in the database
No refined flour or added sugar, unlike a typical pancake
Naturally sweetened only by banana

name: ZITLAS Masala Poha Cutlet
description: Leftover cooked poha shaped into pan-fried cutlets — a genuinely different leftover-rescue recipe using leftover poha rather than rice, roti or dal.
instructions: Mash the leftover poha lightly with onion, rice flour and spices until it holds together.
Shape into small flat cutlets.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve with ketchup or chutney.
why_it_works: Genuinely rescues leftover poha specifically, a food-waste angle not covered elsewhere in the database
Crisping via pan-frying gives a completely different texture from reheated poha
Very low additional cost

name: ZITLAS Bengali Fish Curry Rice Bowl
description: A light Bengali-style fish curry served over warm rice — a regional non-vegetarian breakfast using fish, a protein source not used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Rub the fish fillet with turmeric and a little salt.
Heat mustard oil, temper panch phoron, then saute onion until soft.
Add tomato and cook until pulpy, then add a little water to form a light gravy.
Gently add the fish and simmer 6-8 minutes until just cooked through, being careful not to break it up.
Serve the curry over warm rice.
why_it_works: Fish is a distinct protein source from every other recipe in the database, giving genuine variety for non-vegetarian users
Mustard oil and panch phoron give an authentic Bengali flavour base
Light gravy keeps this suited to a fitness-conscious breakfast rather than a heavy lunch curry

name: ZITLAS Paneer Bhurji Stuffed Capsicum
description: Capsicum halves stuffed with spiced paneer bhurji and lightly steamed — a vegetable-as-vessel format distinct from any bread, rice or roll pairing.
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion, add turmeric and chilli powder, then add paneer and cook 3-4 minutes into a bhurji.
Stuff the paneer bhurji generously into the capsicum halves.
Steam the stuffed capsicum halves in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 6-8 minutes until the capsicum softens slightly but keeps some bite.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Using the vegetable itself as the vessel removes the need for bread or rice entirely
Lower carb than most other paneer bhurji pairings in the database
Visually different, good for a lighter breakfast

name: ZITLAS Vegetable Bread Upma
description: Day-old bread torn into pieces and tossed upma-style with a mustard-curry leaf tempering and vegetables — a bread-based upma distinct from the rava, poha or dalia versions.
ingredients: Whole wheat bread, torn into pieces — 90 g
Mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric — 3 g
instructions: Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute onion and tomato until soft.
Add turmeric and the torn bread pieces, tossing gently on medium heat for 3-4 minutes until well coated and slightly crisp at the edges.
Serve hot immediately, before the bread softens too much.
why_it_works: Uses leftover or day-old bread that would otherwise be wasted, a distinct leftover-rescue angle from the rice, roti or poha versions
Familiar upma tempering technique applied to an unusual base
Very fast, one-pan preparation

name: ZITLAS Soya Chunk Salad Bowl
description: Cold, marinated soya chunks tossed with vegetables in a no-cook salad — distinct from the cooked soya sabzi, frankie or keema preparations elsewhere.
ingredients: Soya chunks, boiled and cooled — 80 g
instructions: Boil the soya chunks briefly, squeeze out excess water, and let cool completely.
Toss the cooled soya chunks with cucumber and tomato.
Dress with lemon juice, a little oil, black pepper and chaat masala.
Chill briefly if possible and serve cold.
why_it_works: Cold salad format is a genuinely different way to eat soya chunks from every cooked preparation elsewhere in the database
No stovetop cooking needed at breakfast time if chunks are pre-boiled the night before
High protein, low calorie

name: ZITLAS Dahi Semiya (Curd Vermicelli)
description: Cooked vermicelli mixed cold into whisked curd with a light tempering — a South Indian cold noodle-like breakfast dish.
instructions: Boil the vermicelli until just tender, drain and cool completely.
Mix the cooled vermicelli into whisked curd along with grated carrot.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in hot oil and pour over the top.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
why_it_works: Cold, curd-based format is genuinely different from the hot Soya Vermicelli Upma in Batch 2
Light and cooling, suited to hot mornings
Simple, familiar South Indian home food

name: ZITLAS Egg Bhurji Dosa
description: Spiced scrambled egg folded inside a plain dosa — combining two familiar breakfast items into one, distinct from a plain or vegetable dosa.
instructions: Saute onion in a little oil, add turmeric and chilli powder, then scramble in the beaten egg until just set; set aside.
Pour dosa batter on a hot tawa and spread into a dosa.
While the top is still slightly wet, spread the cooked egg bhurji over half of it and fold the dosa over.
Cook briefly to crisp the outside, then serve.
why_it_works: Combines two familiar dishes into a single distinct format, different from a plain dosa or a separate egg bhurji
Higher protein than a plain or vegetable dosa
Popular street-food-style combination

name: ZITLAS Peanut Butter Banana Roti Roll
description: A whole wheat roti spread with peanut butter and sliced banana, rolled up — a sweet roll format distinct from the savoury rolls elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Roll out the atta into a roti and dry-roast on a tawa until just cooked, without over-browning.
Spread peanut butter evenly over the warm roti.
Lay banana slices along one edge and roll up tightly.
Slice in half and serve.
why_it_works: First genuinely sweet roll in the database — most rolls are savoury
No refined sugar, sweetened only by banana
Very quick, minimal ingredients

name: ZITLAS Rajma Chaat Bowl
description: Boiled rajma tossed chaat-style with onion, tomato and tangy spices — a cold, no-cook bowl distinct from the cooked rajma paratha or tikki sandwich elsewhere.
instructions: Toss boiled rajma with onion and tomato.
Add lemon juice and chaat masala.
Mix well and eat immediately while the onion stays crisp.
why_it_works: No-cook chaat format is a genuinely different way to eat rajma from the two cooked recipes already in the database
High fiber, filling, and very low active prep time
Good for a rushed morning

name: ZITLAS Paneer Achari Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha with paneer filling spiced with pickle (achaari) masala — a tangy, distinct spice profile from the other paneer parathas in the database.
ingredients: Pickle masala (achaari) or mustard oil pickle spice mix — 8 g
instructions: Mix paneer with onion and achaari pickle masala into a tangy, spiced filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the filling and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Pickle-spiced (achaari) profile is a distinctly different flavour direction from methi, lite or beetroot paneer parathas elsewhere in the database
Tangy spicing needs less added salt or chutney on the side
Popular restaurant-style flavour made at home

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Dhokla
description: A steamed dhokla made from ground moong dal instead of besan or oats — a different pulse base with its own dense, slightly nutty texture.
ingredients: Moong dal, soaked and ground — 120 g
instructions: Grind soaked moong dal with curd and a little water into a thick batter; rest 15 minutes.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently.
Pour into a greased tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares, and temper mustard and sesame seeds in oil poured over the top.
why_it_works: Moong dal delivers meaningfully more protein per serving than a besan-based dhokla
Distinctly denser texture from the lighter besan or oats versions
Steamed, low added fat

name: ZITLAS Sattu Ladoo Bites
description: No-bake bites made from sattu, jaggery and ghee — a solid, portable format distinct from the sattu drink and sattu-curd bowl elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Melt ghee in a kadai on low heat, add sattu and roast for 2-3 minutes until aromatic.
Add jaggery and mix until fully combined into a thick, moist dough.
Cool slightly, then shape into 8 small balls while still warm.
Store in an airtight container for up to a week.
why_it_works: Solid, portable bite format is genuinely different from the drink or bowl formats already using sattu in the database
Very cheap, high-protein grab-and-go option
Batch-made once for the week

name: ZITLAS Soya Chunk Biryani Bowl
description: Rice and soya chunks layered and cooked dum-style with biryani spices — a distinct spice profile and format from the plain pulao or brown rice meal-prep bowl.
instructions: Marinate the rehydrated soya chunks in curd and biryani masala for 10 minutes.
Heat oil, fry sliced onion until golden and set aside half for garnish.
Layer partially-cooked rice with the marinated soya and remaining fried onion in the cooker.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat (dum-style) for 12-15 minutes.
Fluff gently and garnish with the reserved fried onion before serving.
why_it_works: Biryani spicing and dum technique give a distinctly different flavour and texture from the pulao or plain rice-soya recipes elsewhere
Layered cooking method is a genuinely different technique from a one-pot khichdi or pulao
Weekend-special feel while staying vegetarian and high-protein

name: ZITLAS Paneer Frankie Roll
description: A Mumbai-style frankie roll filled with spiced paneer instead of soya, using the same charred-roti technique but a different protein.
instructions: Roll out and roast the atta into a roti on a tawa until slightly charred at the edges.
Pan-sear paneer cubes with pav bhaji masala until lightly browned.
Spread green and tamarind chutney on the roti, add the paneer and sliced onion.
Roll tightly frankie-style and serve immediately.
why_it_works: Same proven frankie format as the Soya Frankie Roll but with paneer, giving users a protein choice within a familiar format
Two chutneys keep the flavour profile distinct from other paneer rolls in the database
Portable for a commute

name: ZITLAS Lauki Paratha with Curd
description: A stuffed paratha filled with grated bottle gourd (lauki) — a high-water, high-fiber vegetable rarely used in breakfast parathas, served with a side of curd for protein.
ingredients: Bottle gourd (lauki), grated and squeezed — 80 g
instructions: Grate the lauki, squeeze out excess water, and mix with ajwain and chilli powder for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the lauki mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with a side of curd.
why_it_works: Lauki is a genuinely different vegetable filling from any other paratha in the database — high water content and mild flavour
Very low calorie filling, good for weight-loss goals
Curd on the side supplies the protein the vegetable itself lacks

name: ZITLAS Egg Toastie Sandwich
description: A sealed, grilled sandwich with a thin egg omelette layer between bread slices — a closed toastie format distinct from an open toast or a wrap.
instructions: Beat the egg with onion and black pepper, and cook a thin, bread-sized omelette in a pan.
Sandwich the omelette between two slices of bread.
Lightly grill the whole sandwich on a tawa with a little oil, pressing down, until both sides are golden and crisp.
Slice and serve.
why_it_works: Sealed, pressed toastie format is a genuinely different texture from an open-faced toast or wrap
Portable and mess-free once cooked
Familiar comfort food with high protein

name: ZITLAS Curd Chana Dosa
description: A dosa batter enriched by blending in boiled chana — raising the protein of the batter itself rather than relying on a filling.
instructions: Blend the boiled chana with a little water into a smooth paste, then mix into the fermented dosa batter along with cumin seeds.
Heat a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until crisp, then flip briefly.
Serve hot with chutney.
why_it_works: Protein is blended into the batter itself, unlike the Protein-Boosted Idli Sambar approach which relies on a side dish
Distinctly different from a plain dosa in both protein content and slightly nutty flavour
Still cooks exactly like a familiar dosa

name: ZITLAS Beetroot Paneer Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha with a paneer and grated beetroot filling — an iron-rich, visually distinct pink filling from any other paneer paratha in the database.
instructions: Mix paneer with grated beetroot, cumin powder and chilli powder for the filling.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the beetroot-paneer mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Beetroot brings iron and a distinct earthy sweetness not present in any other paneer filling in the database
Visually distinctive (pink interior), which helps variety for repeat users
Traditional protein source in a genuinely different vegetable pairing

name: ZITLAS Moong Sprouts Uttapam
description: A thick pancake made from ground sprouted (not just soaked) moong dal with vegetables pressed on top — a different base and texture from any other uttapam or dosa.
instructions: Grind the sprouted (not just soaked) moong with a little water and cumin seeds into a thick batter — sprouting gives a slightly different, nuttier flavour than plain soaked dal.
Heat a tawa, pour a thick ladle of batter and spread only slightly.
Scatter onion and tomato over the top and press gently.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the base is golden, then flip briefly.
Serve hot.
why_it_works: Using sprouted rather than soaked moong changes both the nutrition and flavour meaningfully from other moong-based dosas or cheelas
Thick uttapam format holds toppings better than a thin dosa
Naturally gluten-free

name: ZITLAS Roasted Gram Dal Chutney Sandwich
description: A sandwich spread made from roasted chana dal ground into a coconut-free chutney — a distinct spread from the peanut thecha or chana chaat sandwiches elsewhere.
instructions: Blend roasted chana dal with green chilli, garlic, lemon juice and a little water into a thick, spreadable chutney.
Spread generously between two slices of bread.
Serve as is, or lightly toast the sandwich if preferred.
why_it_works: Coconut-free, low-fat chutney spread that's meaningfully different from peanut- or chana-chaat-based sandwich fillings elsewhere
Genuinely no-cook if eaten untoasted
Very cheap protein spread instead of butter or jam

name: ZITLAS Multi-Veg Paratha with Protein Raita
description: A paratha stuffed with a mix of grated vegetables (carrot, cabbage, bottle gourd), specifically paired with a Greek yogurt raita so the protein comes from the side, not the filling.
instructions: Mix the grated vegetables with ajwain and chilli powder, squeezing out excess water first.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the vegetable mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve with a generous side of Greek yogurt raita — this is where most of the meal's protein comes from.
why_it_works: Deliberately designed so the protein comes from the raita pairing rather than the filling, a distinct nutritional strategy from the protein-stuffed parathas elsewhere
Uses more than one vegetable in the filling instead of just one
Greek yogurt raises the raita's protein well above regular curd

name: ZITLAS Chicken Bhurji Toast
description: Shredded boiled chicken spiced and scrambled bhurji-style, served over toast — a non-vegetarian bhurji variant using real chicken instead of a soya substitute.
instructions: Boil and shred the chicken breast ahead of time.
Heat oil, saute onion and tomato until soft, add turmeric and chilli powder.
Add the shredded chicken and cook 4-5 minutes, breaking it up further into a bhurji-like texture.
Toast the bread and spoon the chicken bhurji over the top.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Genuine lean-meat protein option for non-vegetarian users who want more than eggs at breakfast
Bhurji technique applied to chicken rather than egg, soya or paneer gives real protein-source variety
High protein, low fat when using breast meat

name: ZITLAS Fish Cutlet Sandwich
description: Pan-fried fish cutlets, Kerala-style, sandwiched in toasted bread — a distinct non-vegetarian protein and format from the chicken or egg options elsewhere.
ingredients: Lean fish fillet, boiled and flaked — 100 g
Ginger, green chilli, black pepper — 5 g
instructions: Mix flaked boiled fish with onion, ginger, green chilli and black pepper.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until golden and firm on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Second fish-based recipe in the database, giving non-vegetarian users a real choice beyond chicken and egg
Cutlet-sandwich format is portable, unlike the curry-rice fish preparation
Kerala-style seasoning gives a distinct regional flavour

name: ZITLAS Fenugreek Seed Paneer Chilla
description: A besan chilla batter infused with soaked, ground fenugreek (methi) seeds and paneer — using the seed rather than the leaf, for a distinctly bitter-edged, mineral-rich flavour.
ingredients: Fenugreek seeds, soaked and ground — 5 g
instructions: Soak fenugreek seeds in water for at least 4 hours, then grind to a paste.
Whisk besan with water, the fenugreek paste and turmeric into a smooth batter.
Mix in crumbled paneer.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil, and serve.
why_it_works: Using fenugreek seeds (not leaves) gives a genuinely different, more medicinal flavour profile from the Methi Paneer Paratha elsewhere in the database
Fenugreek seeds are traditionally used for blood sugar support in Indian home remedies
Distinct enough in both ingredient and preparation to stand apart from other chillas

name: ZITLAS Moong Dal Paratha
description: A stuffed paratha filled with whole cooked moong dal, thickened and spiced — a distinct pulse filling from sattu, rajma or soya-based stuffed parathas.
ingredients: Moong dal, cooked and thickened — 90 g
Cumin powder, ginger, green chilli — 5 g
instructions: Cook moong dal with minimal water until soft, then continue cooking uncovered to dry it out into a thick, moist filling; season with cumin, ginger and green chilli.
Knead atta into a dough, stuff with the dal mixture and seal well.
Roll out gently and roast on a tawa with a little oil until golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd.
why_it_works: Whole-dal filling gives a chunkier texture than the smoother sattu or besan-based stuffed parathas
Different legume filling from the Rajma Paratha or Soya Keema Paratha elsewhere
Traditional dal paratha technique, genuinely fitness-relevant due to its protein and fiber load

name: ZITLAS Buckwheat Vegetable Chilla
description: A savoury buckwheat (kuttu) flour chilla loaded with vegetables — distinct from the plain fasting-style Kuttu Pancake with Curd, treated here as a regular protein-and-fiber breakfast.
instructions: Whisk kuttu flour with water into a thick, spreadable batter.
Mix in grated carrot, onion, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Heat a tawa, pour the batter and spread into a thick round (kuttu doesn't spread thin easily).
Cook 2-3 minutes per side with a little oil until firm and lightly browned.
Serve with mint chutney.
why_it_works: Vegetable-loaded savoury version gives kuttu a genuinely different everyday use, separate from its plain fasting-day preparation elsewhere in the database
Gluten-free flour choice
Distinct nutty flavour keeps chilla rotation varied

name: ZITLAS Black Chana Ragda Bowl
description: A wet, tangy black chana curry (ragda) eaten as a warm bowl — a distinct wet-curry chaat format from the drier chana sundal or chana chaat toast.
ingredients: Ragda masala or garam masala, tamarind — 5 g
instructions: Heat oil, saute onion until golden, add tomato and cook until soft.
Add boiled black chana, ragda masala and tamarind with enough water to form a thin, wet gravy.
Simmer 8-10 minutes, mashing a few chana lightly to thicken the gravy naturally.
Serve hot in a bowl, topped with chopped onion if liked.
why_it_works: Deliberately wet, gravy-style consistency is genuinely different from the dry-tossed sundal or the toast-piled chaat elsewhere
Street-food ragda-pattice flavour without the fried pattice
Filling, warming bowl for cooler mornings

name: ZITLAS Paneer Vegetable Kofta Bowl
description: Steamed (not fried) paneer-vegetable kofta balls served in a light tomato gravy bowl — a distinct ball-in-gravy format not used elsewhere in the database.
instructions: Mix grated paneer with grated vegetables and rice flour into a firm dough; shape into small balls.
Steam the balls in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 10 minutes until firm, rather than deep-frying.
Separately, cook tomato with oil and garam masala into a light gravy.
Add the steamed koftas to the gravy just before serving, simmering 2 minutes to warm through.
why_it_works: Steaming instead of deep-frying keeps this meaningfully lighter than a restaurant-style kofta
Ball-and-gravy bowl format is genuinely different from every roll, paratha or bhurji elsewhere
Vegetables are built into the kofta itself, not a side

name: ZITLAS Barley Porridge Bowl
description: A warm porridge made from barley (jau) flour cooked with milk — an uncommon grain choice with a distinct fiber and mineral profile from oats, ragi or rajgira porridges.
instructions: Whisk barley flour into a little cold milk to avoid lumps.
Heat the rest of the milk, add the flour mixture and stir continuously.
Simmer 6-8 minutes until thickened.
Stir in jaggery and cardamom powder, cook 1-2 more minutes, and serve warm.
why_it_works: Barley is a genuinely uncommon breakfast grain in most Indian households, offering different soluble fiber than oats or millets
Same simple porridge technique but a distinctly different base ingredient
Good option for grain variety across the week

name: ZITLAS Soya Chunk Cutlet Sandwich
description: Ground rehydrated soya chunks shaped into pan-fried cutlets and sandwiched in bread — a distinct patty-sandwich format from the loose soya fillings used in rolls or frankies.
ingredients: Soya chunks, rehydrated and ground — 70 g
instructions: Coarsely grind the rehydrated soya chunks and mix with onion, rice flour and garam masala into a firm mixture.
Shape into a flat cutlet.
Pan-fry in oil until crisp and golden on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Toast the bread and sandwich the cutlet inside.
Serve warm.
why_it_works: Patty format holds together for a sandwich, unlike the wet sabzi or dry keema-style soya fillings elsewhere
Genuinely different construction technique from the moong dal or rajma-oats tikki sandwiches
Good lunchbox option

name: ZITLAS Paneer and Vegetable Momos
description: Steamed North-East-Indian-style dumplings filled with grated paneer and finely chopped vegetables — a steamed dumpling format entirely distinct from any roll, roti or rice dish in the database.
instructions: Knead maida with water into a smooth, firm dough; rest 15 minutes.
Mix grated paneer with cabbage, carrot, ginger, garlic and soy sauce for the filling.
Roll small discs of dough, place a spoon of filling in the centre and pleat closed into a momo shape.
Steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle), using a steamer plate, for 10-12 minutes.
Serve hot with a spicy chilli dip.
why_it_works: Steamed dumpling format is genuinely unlike anything else in the database — no roti, rice or roll base at all
Reflects North-East Indian food culture, broadening the database's regional range
Vegetables and protein both folded inside a single bite-sized unit

name: ZITLAS Mixed Sprouts Dhokla
description: A steamed dhokla made from a blend of ground mixed sprouts rather than a single pulse — a fifth distinct dhokla base in the database, using multiple legumes at once.
instructions: Grind mixed sprouts with curd and a little water into a thick batter; rest 15 minutes.
Add eno fruit salt just before steaming and mix gently.
Pour into a greased tin and steam in a pressure cooker (without the whistle) for 12-15 minutes.
Cool slightly, cut into squares, and temper mustard and sesame seeds in oil poured over the top.
why_it_works: Using a blend of sprouted legumes rather than one single pulse gives a broader amino acid profile than any single-pulse dhokla in the database
Distinct texture from the smoother besan or moong dal versions
Steamed, low added fat

name: ZITLAS Corn Cheela
description: A besan chilla batter with coarsely crushed corn kernels mixed in — a distinct texture and natural sweetness from any other chilla in the database.
ingredients: Boiled corn kernels, coarsely crushed — 50 g
instructions: Whisk besan with water into a smooth batter, then mix in crushed corn, cumin seeds and green chilli.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread into a round.
Cook until golden on both sides with a little oil.
Serve with chutney.
why_it_works: Corn adds natural sweetness and a distinct pop of texture not present in any other besan-based chilla here
Kid-friendly flavour, good for a family breakfast rotation
Simple, one-pan, quick preparation

name: ZITLAS Roasted Makhana Chaat Bowl
description: Roasted makhana tossed warm with chopped vegetables and chaat masala — a savoury chaat-style bowl distinct from the yogurt parfait or dry trail-mix uses of makhana elsewhere.
instructions: Dry-roast the makhana in a little oil until crisp, about 4-5 minutes.
Toss the warm roasted makhana with onion, tomato, chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve immediately while the makhana is still crisp.
why_it_works: Third distinct makhana format in the database (yogurt parfait, dry trail mix, now a warm savoury chaat), each genuinely different in preparation and eating experience
Very low calorie, high volume
Quick and needs almost no cleanup

name: ZITLAS Soya Granule Idli
description: Regular idli batter enriched with finely ground soya granules mixed in before steaming — a third distinct protein-boosted idli approach alongside the paneer-stuffed and rava versions elsewhere.
instructions: Mix the finely ground soya granules into the fermented idli batter just before steaming, stirring gently to keep the batter airy.
Pour into greased idli moulds and steam for 10-12 minutes until a knife comes out clean.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in a little oil and drizzle over before serving.
why_it_works: Soya granules blend into the batter itself, giving an even protein distribution rather than a pocket of filling
Distinct from both the paneer-stuffed idli and the vegetable rava idli in construction and protein source
Still fully steamed, no added fat beyond the tempering

name: ZITLAS Multigrain Paratha with Peanut Chutney
description: A paratha made from a multigrain flour blend (not single-grain bajra or wheat), paired specifically with a peanut chutney — different grain base and pairing from the Bajra Roti with Peanut Chutney.
instructions: Knead the multigrain flour into a dough with water; roll out into a paratha.
Roast on a hot tawa with a little oil until golden with brown spots on both sides.
For the chutney, dry-roast peanuts and pound coarsely with garlic, red chilli and salt.
Serve the paratha hot with the peanut chutney.
why_it_works: Multigrain blend (several grains at once) gives a broader fiber and mineral profile than the single-grain Bajra Roti elsewhere
Paratha (with fat worked into layers) is a different texture from a flat roti even with a similar pairing
Same reliable peanut-chutney protein pairing, different grain base

name: ZITLAS Vermicelli Egg Upma
description: Roasted vermicelli upma with scrambled egg folded through — using egg rather than soya as the protein addition, distinct from the Soya Vermicelli Upma in Batch 2.
instructions: Dry-roast the vermicelli until light golden; set aside.
Heat oil, temper mustard seeds and curry leaves, then saute onion and carrot for 3 minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side, crack in the egg and scramble it in the empty space.
Add the roasted vermicelli with hot water (roughly equal volume), mix everything together, and cook covered until the water is absorbed.
why_it_works: Egg-based protein addition gives a genuinely different flavour and texture from the soya-chunk version already in the database
Still cooks in one pan in under 20 minutes
Good option for egg-eating users who don't want soya

name: ZITLAS Paneer Sprouts Salad Bowl
description: A cold, no-cook salad combining cubed paneer with mixed sprouts — distinct from the cooked Sprout Paneer Tikki, this stays entirely raw and dressed simply.
instructions: Toss cubed paneer with mixed sprouts and chopped cucumber.
Dress with lemon juice, black pepper and chaat masala.
Mix gently and eat immediately for the best texture.
why_it_works: Fully raw, no-cook format is a genuinely different way to eat paneer and sprouts together from the cooked tikki version elsewhere
Two protein sources combined with zero cooking
Very quick assembly, good for a rushed morning
